item.title: Michael Looney
item.description: Michael Looney, Ross Road, Killarney, (Co.Kerry) Peacefully at home on the 31st December 2025. Beloved husband of Mary (née Spillane) and dearly loved father of John, Niamh, Lisa, Maura and Brian. Predeceased by his brothers Timmy and Denis (Dee). Michael will be lovingly remembered and sadly missed by his brother Jackie, grandchildren Michaela, Seán, Cathal, Fionn, Ciarán, Síobhra, Mary, Oisín, Evan, Liam, Sinéad and Culann, great granddaughter Fiadh, daughter-in-law Stella, sons-in-law Charlie

item.title: Eight people died on Kerry roads in 2025
item.description: Eight people died on Kerry roads last year, compared to seven who lost their lives in 2024, leaving the Kingdom with the sixth highest death rate per county. Dublin had the highest number of road fatalities in 2025 with 22 deaths; Longford recorded no deaths on its roads last year. That's according to provisional figures released by the Road Safety Authority which says there was a concerning increase in the numbers who died on our roads in 2025. item.title: Surveys informing design of Tralee to Listowel Greenway to be completed during first quarter of new year
item.description: Topographical surveys to inform the design of the Tralee to Listowel Greenway will be completed during the first quarter of the new year. An update on the Tralee to Listowel greenway project was sought by Sinn Féin councillor Paul Daly at the recent Tralee Municipal District meeting. Kerry County Council says Fehilly Timoney have been appointed as consultants and their commission will take the scheme through the statutory consent process. item.title: Maresca parts company with Chelsea
item.description: Enzo Maresca has left Chelsea after a year and a half in charge. Speculation about his future had increased following a run of one win in seven Premier League games. Last month Maresca said the 48 hours before the win over Everton were the worst during his time at the club due to a lack of support for him. Advertisement

item.title: Coventry drop points again but remain 8 points clear
item.description: Coventry remain eight-points clear at the top of the Championship - despite dropping points for the second successive match. Frank Lampard's side were held to a 1-all draw at Charlton - but their promotion rivals Middlesbrough lost 1-nil to Derby. item.title: Mother of UHK's first baby of 2026 works at the hospital
item.description: The first baby to be born in UHK in 2026 is a boy who arrived at 3.22 this morning. Louie Kurian Johns is the first child of Emil Emmanuel and John Kurian who live in Tralee. Louie's mother Emil is a nurse at University Hospital Kerry. Advertisement Emil says she and her husband John are delighted that Louie whose due date was yesterday was born on New Year's Day. She says it's extra special that her son was born in the hospital she works in. Advertisement

item.title: Íarnród Éireann says cameras will be installed at Farranfore and Minish level crossings in coming months
item.description: Íarnród Éireann says cameras will be installed at level crossings in Farranfore and Minish in the coming months. The automatic cameras will take images of motorists who fail to stop at flashing red lights on the level crossings. Offenders will receive an €80 fine and two penalty points. Advertisement Motorists who try to drive though level crossings will be fined €160 and given three penalty points. Last year, nationally, there were 22 collisions with gates at level crossings.
